recon.extraction_guidance: 1. This paper has NO tables - all quantitative data are in figures and must be read graphically. 2. The primary target outcome for meta-analysis is P concentration in shoots and roots from Figure 1d and 1e (P-deficient, wild-type plants only). 3. ALWAYS record nitrogen form (NO3- or NH4+) as a subgroup/moderator because CO2 effect on P concentration is POSITIVE under NO3- and NEGATIVE under NH4+. 4. Use only wild-type data; exclude mutant nr and atnos1 data (Fig. 8). 5. For the main P-deficiency experiment: control = 350 ppm CO2, treatment = 800 ppm CO2, n=5, variance = SD. 6. P-adequate supplementary data (Fig. S1) can also be extracted as a separate observation but note it is P-replete. 7. CO2 control level (350 ppm) is within normal ambient range; elevated CO2 (800 ppm) is higher than typical FACE studies - note this as a potential moderating variable. 8. 'P absorbed per unit weight of roots' (Fig. 1g) is a derived metric (total P / root DW), not a tissue concentration - extract separately from tissue concentrations. 9. Do not extract data from SNP/cPTIO pharmacological treatments (Fig. 6) as these are mechanistic not primary CO2 comparisons.
